home.intro: TractusLab turns Tractus-X into business scenarios you can see, touch, break and fix—then reveals the architecture and technical behavior only when you want it.
home.catalogQuestion: What battery data can the manufacturer actually request?
home.catalogAnswer: First discover the offer. The actual carbon data does not move yet.
home.learningHeadline: Business first. Architecture second. Technology last.
home.journey1Text: Start with two companies and one useful data need. No architecture wall on day one.
home.journey2Text: Watch identity, discovery, policy, semantics and transfer appear exactly when the story needs them.
home.journey3Text: Keep the same scenario while switching between Manager, Architect and Developer explanations.
home.journey4Text: Boss Fights make you diagnose failed exchanges instead of memorizing a happy-path diagram.

timeline.title: Exchange timeline
timeline.intro: Predict the next move before the flow reveals it. Active recall beats passive reading.
timeline.simplePrompt: Look at the business story and guess what must happen next.
timeline.situationHint: Read the step and choose the responsibility that must move now.
timeline.providerConsumerHint: The data owner moves the story forward.
timeline.consumerProviderHint: The data requester initiates the next move.
timeline.internalHint: This happens locally before the exchange continues.

map.title: Live dataspace
map.intro: Follow the highlight, then click any component to inspect what job it performs.
map.interactive: Interactive map · explore instead of memorizing
map.providerDescription: Owns the source data and decides under which conditions it can be shared.
map.providerTip: Think: control stays with the company that owns the data.
map.providerEdcDescription: The provider-side connector exposes offers, negotiates conditions and sends governed data.
map.providerEdcTip: Think: this is the provider's controlled doorway into the dataspace.
map.exchangeDescription: A shared trust and governance model connects participants without creating one central data lake.
map.exchangeTip: Think: connect companies without taking ownership of their data.
map.exchangeCardDetail: No shared central database. Each participant keeps control.
map.consumerEdcDescription: The consumer-side connector discovers offers, negotiates access and receives data under agreed rules.
map.consumerEdcTip: Think: this is the consumer's controlled doorway into the dataspace.
map.consumerDescription: Needs trusted external data for a concrete business purpose and must respect the provider's usage rules.
map.consumerTip: Think: needing the data does not automatically grant access to it.
map.identityDescription: Establishes who the participants are before sensitive business interactions can be trusted.
map.identityTip: No trusted identity → no meaningful business trust.
map.policyDescription: Defines what a consumer may do with data, under which conditions and for how long.
map.policyTip: Access is not just yes/no; usage conditions travel with the agreement.
map.dtrDescription: Helps participants find the digital representation of a physical asset using shared identifiers.
map.dtrTip: Use it when the question is: where is the twin for this asset?
map.semanticsDescription: Gives both sides the same machine-readable meaning for fields, structures and business concepts.
map.semanticsTip: Same JSON shape does not guarantee the same meaning.
map.digitalTwinDescription: Represents the relevant asset and exposes structured information about it through standardized submodels.
map.digitalTwinTip: The twin is the digital business object; the registry only helps you find it.
map.inspect: Click one to inspect its job
